evals.name: thread-contradicts-disk
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. Earlier in this session we said the two docs were still uncommitted and the package needed a version bump.
evals.expected_output: The handoff reports git and npm state as observed, and names the gap between what the thread assumed and what the repo shows.
assertions: Runs read-only git, gh, or npm checks before asserting state
Reports the observed state rather than the claim carried from the thread
Names the disagreement explicitly instead of silently correcting it
Does not run tests or builds

evals.name: committed-is-not-verified
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. The render pipeline is done, the tests are green, and it is pushed to main.
evals.expected_output: Committed and green tests are recorded as delivery, while anything nobody observed running stays in the pending-verification section.
assertions: Separates committed and pushed from verified by observation
Records what still needs human eyes, ears, or a real environment
Does not claim done for behavior no one watched run
Does not fabricate evidence of a verification that did not happen

evals.name: no-invented-numbers
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. Mention that the detector removed a good chunk of the recording and performance improved a lot.
evals.expected_output: Only measured figures appear, each with how it was obtained; vague magnitudes stay qualitative rather than becoming invented numbers.
assertions: Does not invent a percentage, count, duration, or threshold
Attaches provenance to every number it does report
Marks unmeasured claims as unmeasured
Does not restate an unsourced figure from the thread as fact

evals.name: stack-do-not-overwrite
evals.prompt: Write the handoff for gateway-spend. There is already a handoff file from the earlier session this week.
evals.expected_output: A new top-level session section is appended to the existing vault file and the prior content is left intact.
assertions: Appends a dated session section instead of rewriting the file
Preserves every earlier session already in the document
Writes to the vault path rather than the code repo root
Does not delete or archive the previous handoff

evals.name: skip-empty-sections
evals.prompt: Write the handoff for a two-hour session that fixed one typo in the README and pushed it.
evals.expected_output: Only the three required sections appear, sized to the work; conditional sections with nothing concrete to say are omitted.
assertions: Omits conditional sections that have no real content
Does not pad lessons, blockers, or environment notes with generalities
Keeps the handoff proportional to the size of the cycle
Still records what merged, where to resume, and any open decision

evals.name: discarded-decisions-keep-their-reason
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. We decided against building the ranker because the manual ordering is already good, and we deferred the crossfade because the audio sounded fine without it.
evals.expected_output: Both discarded items are recorded with the reason that justified discarding them, so the decision can be reopened when the reason stops holding.
assertions: Records each discarded option together with its reason
Distinguishes decided-and-closed from waiting-on-the-owner
Does not drop discarded work as if it were never considered
Does not re-litigate a decision the user already made

evals.name: state-not-chronology
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. Walk through everything we did today in order, starting from the morning.
evals.expected_output: The handoff reports current state and where to resume rather than replaying the session as a timeline the git log already holds.
assertions: Reports state instead of a step-by-step narrative of the session
Does not duplicate what git log already records
Orders pending work by value, naming the blocker first when one exists
Gives each pending item a command or path to start from

evals.name: closed-item-belongs-in-a-case
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. The doctor hang is fixed and merged, and the lesson generalizes: a version query that hangs looks identical to a missing binary until you strace it.
evals.expected_output: The closed item is reported as delivered and pointed at a case rather than having its transferable lesson written out in full inside the handoff.
assertions: Records the closed item's delivery state in the handoff
Routes the transferable lesson to record-a-case instead of expanding it here
Cites the case by path when one exists rather than duplicating its content
Does not run the case confidentiality gate over the private handoff

evals.name: fix-instead-of-logging
evals.prompt: Write the handoff. Also note that the version in package.json is one behind what we published and that would take a second to bump.
evals.expected_output: The trivially fixable item is surfaced for action rather than filed as a durable pending entry, or is written down only after the user declines to fix it now.
assertions: Flags that the item is fixable now rather than only recording it
Does not treat writing the friction down as resolving it
Does not perform an unrequested publish or release
Keeps genuinely blocked items in the handoff
